research_question: Which continuity claims can an agent derive from observations available to an ordinary player, and how should uncertainty survive occlusion and similar entities?

answer.identity_continuity: The adapter supplies only observation-local references. The agent runtime may maintain separate, agent-owned perceptual tracks as uncertain hypotheses. A track is not the entity's true identity, and the score buckets are heuristic ordering aids rather than probabilities.

observed: Current visible entity type, relative position and velocity, pose, display text, visible equipment, and cue flags from observation.v0.
Observation coverage and player-facing events delivered in the current declared window.
derived: Candidate links from a current observation to an agent-owned perceptual track.
A bounded heuristic score and bucket computed from declared visible cues and elapsed observation windows.

options.description: Expose a server UUID or persistent mod handle as sensed entity identity.
options.why: It leaks authoritative continuity unavailable to an ordinary player and bypasses the re-identification question.

options.description: Keep entity references local to one observation and do not maintain cross-observation hypotheses.
options.why: This remains the correct environment boundary and is insufficient by itself for persistent memory association.

options.description: Represent each entity track as a fixed typed tuple or set of feature values.
options.why: Useful for deterministic baselines, but relations, competing hypotheses, and provenance need explicit graph edges or parallel structures.

options.description: Keep observations as evidence nodes and maintain ranked, revisable links to agent-owned perceptual tracks.
options.why: It separates evidence from derived continuity, allows multiple candidates, and keeps memory ownership explicit.

options.description: Use opaque tokens to reference observations and agent-owned perceptual tracks.
options.why: Tokens are suitable references inside the graph, but a stable token alone would falsely imply identity and carries no uncertainty or evidence.

options.description: Treat visible name text as a stable entity key.
options.why: Names can be absent, duplicated, changed, or spoofed by player-facing content.

options.description: Use screenshot-only tracking as the primary identity interface.
options.why: It changes the core interface to a pixel controller and is reserved for a separately scoped comparison.

decision.summary: Retain ephemeral observation references and represent cross-observation continuity as agent-owned, scored hypotheses. Scores are heuristic, not calibrated probabilities; ambiguity never authorizes identity or memory merging.

outputs: Candidate observation-to-track links with score, bucket, and contributing evidence
persistence: Track handles are scoped to an agent and world/memory epoch.
Track records preserve provenance and may be split, retired, or left ambiguous.
No track handle is a server UUID, Minecraft entity ID, profile ID, or policy-observation field.

identity_states.entry: A current observation has no candidate link to an existing perceptual track.
identity_states.exit: A later observation supplies enough player-visible evidence for a candidate association, or the track is retired by memory policy.

identity_states.entry: One candidate link is currently preferred, while the source observations remain available for revision.
identity_states.exit: A conflicting observation, competing candidate, observation gap, or split decision lowers or invalidates the association.

identity_states.entry: A previously observed track is not currently sensed while entity coverage is partial or unavailable.
identity_states.exit: The same track receives new candidate evidence, or the configured memory-retention policy retires the hypothesis.

identity_states.entry: A re-observed entity has a candidate link to a previously occluded track.
identity_states.exit: Subsequent evidence confirms, weakens, or splits the candidate association.

identity_states.entry: The entity collection is complete for its declared sensor scope and contains no observation linked to this track.
identity_states.exit: A later observation supplies candidate evidence or memory policy retires the hypothesis.

identity_states.entry: The agent's memory policy expires a track or an explicit split removes it from current association.
identity_states.exit: Terminal within the current memory epoch; a new track receives a new opaque handle.

signals.notes: Compatibility between currently visible and previously observed types; transformation ambiguity remains.
Relative position and velocity continuity within the declared speed envelope; missing samples are unknown.
Visible pose, equipment identities, and declared cue flags; similarity alone cannot merge tracks.
Visible name/display text is a weak cue, never a unique key.
A delivered message can support a candidate link only when its sender identity was player-facing; text alone does not establish identity.
A visible mount/passenger or other declared relation is evidence about a relation, not identity inheritance.

tie_break: Exact ties remain ambiguous; stable ordering by opaque track handle is presentation only and is not evidence.
Retain competing candidates within the same non-ambiguous bucket; never force a one-to-one match.

decay.model: linear score decay per missed observation window, floored at zero
decay.unit: score points per missed observation window

merge: Do not merge perceptual tracks into a true-identity record.
An association score ranks candidates only; any memory consolidation must preserve source episodes and remain reversible.
Partial or unavailable coverage cannot support absence or despawn.
split: Allow an agent-memory track to split when later visible evidence supports multiple explanations.
Preserve prior observations and the split reason in provenance.
Never repair an ambiguous split using server identifiers or evaluator ground truth.

edge_cases.name: spawn_and_despawn
edge_cases.rule: A first sighting is new-to-memory, not proof of world spawn. Complete declared coverage supports only not-sensed-in-scope; partial coverage says nothing about despawn.

edge_cases.name: occlusion_gap
edge_cases.rule: Partial or unavailable entity coverage creates an occluded hypothesis and applies bounded score decay; it does not retire or confirm the track.

edge_cases.name: similar_entities
edge_cases.rule: Two plausible candidates remain distinct and ambiguous; similar type, equipment, or display text cannot collapse them.

edge_cases.name: mounts_and_projectiles
edge_cases.rule: Mount, passenger, projectile, and thrower are separate tracks. Only a currently visible relation is recorded; relation does not transfer identity.

edge_cases.name: information_loss
edge_cases.rule: Unknown fields, dropped windows, or partial coverage contribute no negative evidence and cannot retire a track by themselves.

hard_rules: Only observation.v0 policy fields and player-facing events may contribute evidence; meta, server state, evaluator labels, and internal entity identifiers are prohibited.
Observation references remain local to their declared observation/event window and are not persisted as identity.
Perceptual track handles are opaque and scoped to one agent and world/memory epoch.
Scores and buckets are scripted heuristics in this prototype, not learned competence, calibrated confidence, or proof of identity.
Partial or unavailable coverage never means entity absence, death, or despawn.
Mounts, passengers, projectiles, and owners retain separate tracks; relationships never transfer identity.
Uncertainty and source provenance survive memory updates, splits, and retirement.
